title: Tool and holder bodies as a spun profile: show them revolved in simulation, and turn an imported STEP body into an editable half-profile (DXF with a centreline)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
Requested by the maintainer.

## 1. Simulation shows the tool and holder as spun profiles
While simulating, draw the **tool and its holder as revolved bodies**: the half-profile spun about the spindle axis, at the tool's position and orientation each frame. Today's simulation doesn't show them as solids. Use the same profile the collision laws judge (the revolved envelope, #368), so what you see is what is checked.

## 2. Imported tool bodies and holders become an editable half-profile
When a tool body or holder is imported as **STEP**, convert it to a **2D half-profile on a centreline** (the meridian of the revolved envelope: radius against height along the tool axis). Store it as a **DXF**, with the centreline as its own entity/layer, so the profile can be edited (in the spun-profile editor, #93) and re-exported.

- Only the half-profile is editable, and the body is always its revolution about the centreline.
- Conversion should be conservative: the profile is the outer envelope (max radius at each height), never smaller than the solid, so collision checks stay safe. Non-revolved features (flats, coolant holes, the holder's drive slots) are enveloped, never cut away. Say so in the UI.
- Refuse by name when the STEP body has no clear axis (axis detection/alignment: #370) instead of guessing one.
- A tool/holder can also be **imported directly as a DXF half-profile** (a centreline plus an open profile on one side of it).
- DXF read/write is our own, written from the published DXF reference (entities `LINE`, `ARC`, `LWPOLYLINE`, layers). The minimum needed is lines and arcs, with a named refusal for anything else (splines, unclosed profiles that cross the centreline).

## Related
- #93 spun (revolved-profile) design editor for tool and holder shapes: the editor for these profiles.
- #361 import vendor STEP tool models; #368 a vendor holder judged by its revolved envelope (closed); #370 align a vendor STEP by its tool coordinate systems; #371 pick tip and axis on an imported body (closed).
- Fixtures get the same treatment in a sibling issue.

## Done means
- The simulation draws the tool and holder as revolved solids from their profiles (structural/paint assertion where possible, hand-tested by the maintainer; no snapshot PNG changes).
- Importing a STEP holder produces a DXF half-profile with a centreline, and the envelope encloses the original solid (a test samples the STEP mesh and checks every point lies inside the revolved profile).
- A DXF half-profile imports as a tool/holder body; malformed DXF (no centreline, spline, crossing profile) is a named error in a test, never a panic.
- Round trip: STEP → DXF → body → DXF is stable within tolerance.
